issue.summary: Same supplier on 2 different payment terms across ERPs

plan.diagnosis: Keystone Components KG is configured with inconsistent payment terms across NetSuite (NT30) and SAP (Net 30), representing semantically identical 30-day terms but with different nomenclature. This mismatch across the two ERPs covering $8,178,150 in annual spend creates reconciliation complexity, potential duplicate payment risk, and prevents unified cash flow forecasting and working capital optimization.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct immediate three-way reconciliation between AP teams in NetSuite and SAP to identify any duplicate payments or timing discrepancies for Keystone Components KG invoices over the past 90 days

Standardize payment term master data to 'Net 30' in both SAP (vendor master LFB1 ZTERM field) and NetSuite (vendor record payment terms) for Keystone Components KG across all company codes and subsidiaries
remedy_steps.owner: Master Data Governance Lead with ERP System Administrators

remedy_steps.step: Implement vendor master data governance rule in MDM system to enforce single payment term standard ('Net 30' format) for all future supplier records and flag any deviations during supplier onboarding or maintenance
Negotiate with Keystone Components KG for early payment discount (2/10 Net 30) to capture working capital benefit on the $8.2M spend base, targeting 1.5-2% savings
Update PO templates and supplier communication protocols to reference standardized payment terms and establish quarterly vendor statement reconciliation process for Keystone Components KG

plan.expected_impact: Elimination of payment term discrepancies will prevent potential duplicate payments and enable capture of early payment discounts worth approximately $122,672 to $163,563 annually (1.5-2% of $8,178,150 spend).
kpis: Payment term standardization completion rate (target: 100% by Week 2)
Invoice processing cycle time reduction for Keystone Components KG (baseline vs. post-remedy)
Early payment discount capture rate (target: 60% of eligible invoices)
Vendor master data quality score (zero payment term mismatches across ERPs)
Days Payable Outstanding (DPO) consistency variance between NetSuite and SAP (target: <2 days)
risks: Supplier resistance to payment term renegotiation may delay early payment discount implementation
Historical invoice data discrepancies between ERPs may reveal unreconciled payments requiring manual resolution
Lack of integrated MDM system may allow future payment term drift if governance processes are not enforced
Cash flow impact if early payment discount terms are adopted without treasury approval and liquidity planning
erp_actions: SAP: Update vendor master LFB1-ZTERM to 'Net 30' for Keystone Components KG across all company codes; remove any variant terms (ZT30, 30DN, etc.)
NetSuite: Standardize vendor record payment terms field to 'Net 30' for Keystone Components KG across all subsidiaries
SAP: Configure payment term 'Net 30' with 2% early payment discount (ZTERM = 2/10 Net 30) if negotiation succeeds, using transaction code OBB8
NetSuite: Create corresponding discount payment term '2% 10 Net 30' in Lists > Accounting > Payment Terms if supplier agreement is finalized
Coupa (if integrated): Update supplier profile payment terms to 'Net 30' and enable automated 3-way PO matching to prevent invoice discrepancies
All ERPs: Add data validation rule in vendor master maintenance to flag any payment term entry that deviates from approved standard list (Net 30, Net 45, Net 60, 2/10 Net 30)
